fields.ic_name: Single Edge Nibble Transmission (SENT, SAE J2716)
fields.topology_type: Point-to-point single-wire link: one smart sensor (transmitter) drives one ECU (receiver) over a single signal wire. There is no bus, no multi-drop, and no addressing in basic SENT; each sensor has its own SENT wire to the ECU.

supported_topologies.name: Point-to-point
supported_topologies.description: One sensor -> one ECU over one signal wire (plus supply and ground).

supported_topologies.name: SENT-SPC
supported_topologies.description: Synchronous ECU-triggered exchange; the trigger pulse width selects a channel (addressable).

master_slave_role_summary.description: Encodes sensor data as nibble pulses and transmits SENT frames; the only talker in basic SENT.
Decodes the nibble stream, validates the CRC, and consumes the data; in SENT-SPC it also drives the master trigger pulse.

fields.interconnect_role: SENT is a single-wire sensor-to-ECU link. Data flows one way (sensor to ECU) as pulse-width nibble timing; the optional SENT-SPC variant lets the ECU trigger and address the sensor on the same wire.

ordering_guarantees.frame: Frames are transmitted in order; each is self-delimited by its 56-tick calibration pulse.
ordering_guarantees.nibble: Nibbles are ordered status -> data -> CRC within a frame.
ordering_guarantees.slow_channel: Slow-channel bits accumulate in frame order.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: SENT is not memory-mapped; it is a timed pulse stream on a single wire. There is no address space — one sensor per wire (basic SENT); SENT-SPC selects a data channel by trigger-pulse width.

device_classification.transmitter: Smart sensor that emits SENT frames.
device_classification.receiver: ECU that decodes the nibble stream.
device_classification.spc_master: ECU that drives the SENT-SPC master trigger pulse.
